sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English podcast.
My name is Emily.
I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Slovakia.
Slovakia is a small and beautiful country
in Central Europe.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Slovakia?
Slovakia is in Central Europe.
It is next to Czech Republic, Austria, Hungary, Ukraine,
and Poland.
It has mountains, forests, lakes, and castles.
Slovakia is a landlocked country.
It has no sea.
What is the capital city of Slovakia?
The capital city is Bratislava.
Bratislava is near the Danube River.
It is close to the borders with Austria and Hungary.
Bratislava has a beautiful castle on a hill,
an old town with narrow streets,
modern buildings, shops, and cafes.
Other cities in Slovakia include
Koshits, Prasov, and Gelina.
How many people live in Slovakia?
About five.
Four million people live in Slovakia.
Many people live in cities and towns.
Others live in small villages in the countryside or mountains.
Slovakia is part of the European Union and uses the euro.
What language do people speak in Slovakia?
People speak Slovak.
Slovak is the official language of the country.
Some people also speak Czech, very similar to Slovak,
Hungarian, Romani, German, or Ukrainian in some regions.
English, especially younger people, and in tourist areas.
What is the weather like in Slovakia?
Slovakia has four seasons.
Spring, cool with flowers and green trees.
Summer, warm and sunny, great for hiking.
Autumn, colorful, and cooler.
Winter, cold with snow in many areas.
In winter, people like to go skiing in the mountains.
What does Slovakia look like?
Slovakia is a country with.
The high tatras, tall, snowy mountains,
forests and meadows, caves and rivers,
castles and historic towns.
There are many national parks and hiking trails.
Nature is clean and peaceful.
What animals live in Slovakia?
Slovakia has many wild animals like bears, wolves,
and lynx in the forest, deer, foxes, and wild boars,
eagles, owls, and other birds.
You can also see sheep, goats, and cows in the mountains.
What do people eat in Slovakia?
Slovak food is warm, hardy, and often made at home.
People eat, potatoes, cabbage, and bread,
meat, cheese, and soup.
Popular dishes, Brindsovej Halushki,
potato dumplings with sheep, cheese, and bacon,
national dish, Capasnica, cabbage soup with sausage,
goulash, meat stew with paprika,
Zimiyakovej Plaki, potato pancakes,
kolacha, sweet pastries.
People also enjoy honey, plums, and herbal tea.
What do people drink in Slovakia?
People drink water, tea, and coffee,
milk and fruit juice,
kofala, a local soft drink, similar to cola.
Adults may drink beer, wine, or slavavica, plum brandy.
Drinks are often served warm in winter and cold in summer.
What is life like in Slovakia?
Life in Slovakia is quiet, friendly, and family-focused.
People enjoy nature, traditions, and community life.
In cities, people go to work, school, and shops.
In villages, many people grow food,
keep animals, and enjoy the outdoors.
What are some holidays and traditions in Slovakia?
Christmas, with dinner, songs, and a Christmas tree Easter,
with painted eggs and fun water traditions.
Slovak National Uprising Day, August 29th,
Independence Day, January 1st,
all Saints Day, November 1st, with candles and flowers.
People wear traditional clothes at festivals,
and enjoy folk music and dancing.
Some fun facts about Slovakia.
Slovakia has over 100 castles.
The high tatras are shared with Poland.
The Slovak language uses accents like atchi and jish.
There are many hot springs and spas.
The flag is white, blue, and red, with a cross on a mountain.
Now you know many things about Slovakia.
You know where it is, what people speak, and what they eat.
You learned about the nature, traditions, and daily life.
Great work.
I am Emily.
Goodbye.
Or as they say in Slovak,
Dovidenia.
